prompt: Reading the item at position 1,000 takes the same time as reading position 1.
why: Position 1,000 is found by arithmetic, not by stepping through 999 items, so the cost doesn't depend on where you look. Same cost at any size is O(1).

prompt: Checking a hash set takes about the same time whether it holds 10 names or 10 million.
tells: whether it holds 10 names or 10 million
why: A hash set computes where the name would be and checks only there. The work stays about the same as the set grows, which is O(1).

prompt: Pushing a plate onto a stack doesn't depend on how many plates are already there.
why: Pushing only touches the top of the stack; the plates underneath are never looked at. The cost doesn't change with size, so it's O(1).

prompt: Peeking at the front of a line is one step, however long the line is.
tells: one step, however long the line is
why: Peeking reads one known spot, the front, and ignores everyone behind. One step regardless of length is O(1).

prompt: Getting the first element of a list of a billion items is instant.
why: The first element is always in the same place, so reaching it takes one step even with a billion items. That's constant time, O(1).
trap: A billion items doesn't change the cost.

prompt: Adding one to a counter takes one step no matter how big the count is.
tells: no matter how big the count is
why: Adding one is a single operation on a single number; how large the number is doesn't add work. That's O(1).
trap: Bigger numbers don't take longer here.
